title: subpoena-witness line
description: One line of a witness file: one exec as the kernel saw it, one statement a database witness saw, or a record that opens or closes a capture window. A line with a record field is a record; otherwise a line with an event field is a row line; any other line is an exec. See docs/ports.md (W). Readers ignore fields they do not know; existing fields keep their name and meaning.

time.description: When the exec was seen, when the statement's outcome became known, or when the record was written (RFC 3339, UTC).

pid.description: PID in the process's own PID namespace.

ppid.description: Parent PID in the process's own PID namespace.

host_pid.description: PID in the initial PID namespace.

comm.description: Kernel task name, at most 15 bytes.

exe.description: The path passed to execve; may be relative.

cgroup.description: cgroup path without the hierarchy root, root-most first, at most 8 elements, such as subpoena/<trace id>.

trace_id.description: The session's trace ID, read from its cgroup name. Present only for execs inside a session cgroup.

attribution.description: How the line was tied to a trace. On an exec, present exactly when trace_id is. On a row line always destination: it holds for every trace.

record.description: start: the witness is attached and capturing. stop: it has stopped; healthy says whether the capture between start and stop is complete.

healthy.description: On a stop record: true only if no kernel events were lost and no read or write failed.

error.description: On an unhealthy stop record: what went wrong.

event.description: Row lines only: the kind of event.

conn.description: The witness's number for the connection, from 1.

dest.description: The address the application connected to.

statement.description: SQL text as sent, cut at 8 KiB; empty when none was seen. Never bound values.

tables.description: Tables written, as named, with quotes removed and unquoted parts lower case. A reader must treat an empty list on a write as every table.

opaque.description: The witness could not tell what the statement writes: it counts against every table.

rows.description: Rows the server said it changed, or -1 if its reply gave no usable count. Zero is no effect; a line without this field is an error.

outcome.description: read: writes nothing. committed: the server committed it. rolled_back and failed: not an effect. unknown: its fate was not seen, and the file is a capture fault.
